question: Which group of elements constitutes a triad?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Li(6.9), Na(23.0), K(39.1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dobereiner's Triads:**

 
 
• **​** In the early 19th century, German chemist Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner observed a pattern in the properties of certain groups of elements. He noticed that some elements could be grouped into sets of three, called triads, based on their similar chemical and physical properties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Similar Properties: **The elements within a triad exhibited striking similarities in their chemical behavior. For example, chlorine, bromine, and iodine are all halogens, a group of highly reactive non-metals.
 
• **Atomic Mass Relationship: **The most significant observation was that the atomic mass of the middle element in the triad was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
 
• **In the case of chlorine, bromine, and iodine:**
 
 
• Atomic mass of chlorine: 35.45
 
• Atomic mass of bromine: 79.90
 
• Atomic mass of iodine: 126.90
 
 
 
• Average of chlorine and iodine: (35.45 + 126.90) / 2 = 81.17
 
• Limitations: While Dobereiner's triads provided an early attempt at classifying elements, they had limitations. Not all elements could be neatly organized into triads, and the concept didn't fully explain the periodic trends observed in elemental properties.
